item.title: Architect Labs introduces Frostbite, a new AI-designed CPU architecture with a novel instruction set achieving 4.59x performance-per-watt over modern superscalar CPUs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Architect Labs has developed Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU architecture designed and verified autonomously by AI systems, which introduces a new instruction set based on interaction nets. This design enables local computation steps with explicit dependencies and unique value ownership, resulting in a significant performance-per-watt improvement compared to traditional CPUs. Frostbite's AI-driven process iterated through compiler, ISA, architecture, microarchitecture, RTL, verification, and final layout stages without human architectural priors. The architecture exploits inherent parallelism and reduces power and area costs by eliminating shared mutable state and complex cache coherence, achieving a 4.59x gain on a diverse set of workloads compared to a modern silicon-proven superscalar CPU. This approach suggests potential fundamental shifts in chip design across various classes as AI capabilities advance.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI solves two longstanding open problems in black hole physics, completing a 20-year-old calculation and determining exact limits in quantum gravity models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic's AI system Claude has solved two significant open problems in theoretical physics related to black holes and quantum gravity. It completed a complex calculation initiated over 20 years ago, confirming that a sudden phase transition associated with black hole formation persists even when spacetime lacks a definite shape. Claude also determined the exact limit of a key technique used to test candidate quantum gravity theories in simplified two-dimensional universes. The first problem involved verifying whether the abrupt phase transition observed in black hole formation under general relativity remains sharp in regimes where spacetime becomes quantum and blurry. Claude achieved this by independently performing and cross-checking nearly all parts of the calculation. The second problem addressed the bootstrap method used to rule out inconsistent quantum gravity theories by setting ceilings on black hole masses; Claude identified a missed pattern in numerical results and applied mathematical techniques to establish the precise theoretical limit. These breakthroughs provide new insights into the quantum nature of black holes and help narrow the search for a unified theory of quantum gravity. Claude's work demonstrates the potential of AI to tackle complex problems in fundamental physics that have resisted solution for decades.

item.title: DeepMind explores potential developments beyond artificial general intelligence toward artificial superintelligence and its implications [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: DeepMind examines the future trajectory of AI beyond artificial general intelligence (AGI), considering the possibility of artificial superintelligence (ASI) that could outperform human experts across a wide range of tasks. The essay discusses the continuum of intelligence from human-level AGI to theoretical upper limits, highlighting the largely uncharted space of advanced superintelligent systems. The analysis includes factors driving AI progress such as improvements in hardware manufacturing, algorithmic efficiency, and increased investment in AI compute resources, which together have accelerated AI capabilities and reduced costs. DeepMind emphasizes the need to map potential paths from AGI to ASI and develop reliable methods to track AI progress, given the profound scientific, economic, and societal impacts that ASI could have.

item.title: Pete Warden discusses local AI capabilities, open models, voice interfaces, and emerging hardware trends in AI inference [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Pete Warden, co-creator of Moonshine Voice and experienced deep learning engineer, explains why AI is increasingly running locally rather than in the cloud. He covers the progress of open-weight models, challenges of running AI on laptops and browsers, and the potential for low-latency speech models to improve voice interfaces. Warden also addresses the economics of local AI, privacy concerns, and the shift from GPU-centric hardware to new approaches for AI inference. He highlights the importance of latency in voice AI, the role of specialized versus end-to-end models, and how enterprises may need more control over AI deployments as local AI becomes more capable.

item.title: Report: AI adoption in China is accelerating job losses amid an ongoing employment downturn [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Artificial intelligence technologies are contributing to a worsening job slump in China, intensifying existing employment challenges across various sectors. The integration of AI is accelerating workforce reductions and reshaping labor market dynamics in the country.

item.title: Apple is hiring engineers to develop an AI agent capable of browsing the web, working across apps, and performing multi-step tasks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Apple is developing an AI agent designed to perform a variety of tasks including web browsing, app integration, code writing, and service calls, according to a job listing seeking an engineer to lead this project. The role involves collaboration with teams across Siri, UI Frameworks, and Apple Foundation Models divisions, indicating an expansion of Siri's agentic capabilities. The AI agent aims to coordinate complex tasks across multiple tools such as browsers, documents, terminals, and APIs, reflecting Apple's effort to compete with similar AI assistants from Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Upcoming updates like iOS 27.3 will allow developers to integrate Siri AI into all apps, broadening its functionality across the Apple ecosystem.

item.title: Google integrates AI into search advertising to enhance ad targeting and user experience [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google is changing its search advertising strategy by incorporating artificial intelligence technologies to improve how ads are targeted and to enhance the overall user experience on its search platform. This integration represents a significant shift in Google's approach to search ads, leveraging AI capabilities to optimize ad delivery and relevance.

item.title: PsyFi integrates AI financial coaching with bank data verification to enhance accuracy of dollar amount insights [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: PsyFi has developed an AI-powered financial wellness platform that cross-references AI-generated dollar amounts with actual bank records to ensure accuracy and reliability. The platform offers features such as cash flow analysis, spending categorization, investment insights, and behavioral finance coaching. The system integrates financial data through services like Plaid and Flinks, supports multiple currencies, and uses AI agents to provide personalized financial advice. PsyFi's approach includes rigorous testing and security measures, aiming to deliver a resilient platform that connects users' financial patterns with emotional and behavioral insights.

item.title: Developer uses AI to autonomously build a web browser from scratch in Rust, targeting specific websites without reusing existing browser engines [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A developer has been running an experiment where an AI agent autonomously builds a web browser from scratch using Rust, aiming to support specific websites like BBC, Hacker News, and GitHub. The AI handles all technical decisions independently, without copying code from existing browsers or reusing established browser engines, focusing instead on a clean-room implementation guided by functional requirements. The project, called SWB, restricts the AI from using existing browser-specific engines or JavaScript platforms but allows general-purpose libraries. The AI tests its implementation by comparing behavior with browsers like Chromium and iteratively improves the browser to meet the specified page rendering goals. The developer provides only product-level input, letting the AI control the entire software development lifecycle for this complex project.

item.title: HAProxy lead developer discusses challenges and potential of AI tools in finding bugs in open source software, highlighting access restrictions and report quality issues [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The lead developer of HAProxy and member of the Linux Kernel security team shares his experience with AI-assisted security reports in open source projects, noting both impressive bug discoveries and the prevalence of incomplete, low-value reports. He emphasizes the importance of human validation alongside AI findings and describes efforts to improve report relevance by documenting threat models for Linux Kernel and HAProxy. Despite access to advanced AI models like Anthropic's Mythos being limited due to strict verification and administrative barriers, the team managed to obtain some Mythos-generated reports, which were difficult to use due to poor formatting and lack of reproducer code. The developer also experimented with less capable models to interpret these reports and propose fixes, though challenges remain in distinguishing real defects from false positives without sufficient context. The article highlights ongoing issues with AI tool accessibility for legitimate defensive work and the need for better alignment between AI-generated security findings and developer workflows to enhance open source software security effectively.

item.title: Report: Elite AI researchers use cigarette smoking as a social signal of belief in imminent superintelligence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A report discusses how some elite AI researchers have taken up cigarette smoking as a way to signal their strong belief in the imminent arrival of superintelligent AI and its transformative effects. This behavior is framed as a costly social signal demonstrating commitment to the AI future despite known health risks and social stigma. The article also touches on rumors of espionage involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's alleged extra-marital relationship with a Chinese spy, suggesting that access to Nvidia GPUs is critical for training frontier AI models and that such espionage efforts aim to help China keep pace with AI advancements. Additional commentary explores social signaling practices in tech and finance as forms of costly displays of status or belief.

item.title: Google DeepMind AI accurately predicts Hurricane Melissa's path and Category 5 strength ahead of landfall in Jamaica [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google DeepMind developed an AI weather model that accurately forecasted Hurricane Melissa's trajectory and its intensification to a Category 5 hurricane before it made landfall in Jamaica. This AI approach provided clearer predictions compared to traditional models, which showed significant disagreement on the storm's path and strength a week prior to landfall. The AI model uses historical weather data to perform rapid ensemble forecasts, potentially extending early warning times for disaster preparedness. Experts caution that while this case validates AI's potential in meteorology, further testing across diverse extreme weather events and data-sparse regions is needed to confirm its reliability and integration with traditional forecasting methods.

item.title: Researchers analyze the content-geometry tradeoff in world models using JEPA to learn latent maps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This paper explores the tradeoff between content representation and geometric structure in world models, focusing on how Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) learn latent spatial maps. The study investigates the balance between capturing detailed content and preserving geometric consistency in learned representations, which is crucial for tasks involving spatial understanding and prediction. The findings provide insights into designing more effective world models that integrate content and geometry for improved performance in AI systems.

item.title: NostrPulse launches open-source Bitcoin Lightning and Cashu eCash MCP server for autonomous AI agent micropayments and anti-Sybil protection [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: NostrPulse has released an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables autonomous AI agents to perform machine-to-machine micropayments using Bitcoin Lightning and Cashu eCash. The platform integrates decentralized reputation and anti-Sybil mechanisms to provide Stripe-like payment settlement and fraud protection for AI clients such as Claude Desktop and Cursor. The system supports zero-code integration, a TypeScript SDK for autonomous wallets with spending limits, and interactive testing tools. It also offers optimized profiles for small language models and a reference implementation for decentralized agent-to-agent negotiation and micro-commerce. NostrPulse aims to address vulnerabilities in open agentic systems by combining decentralized payment rails with trust scoring and adaptive spending controls.

item.title: Meta says it is reevaluating its 2030 net-zero emissions target due to increased energy demands from AI infrastructure buildout [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Meta announced it is reconsidering its goal to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2030 because of the growing energy requirements associated with its artificial intelligence development. The company reported a 45% increase in net carbon equivalent emissions in 2025, reaching 11.8 million metric tons, and cited complexities in achieving its original sustainability timeline amid AI infrastructure expansion. Meta's 2030 net-zero target, set in 2020 to align with the Paris Agreement, involves eliminating emissions across its value chain and purchasing carbon removal credits where necessary. The company acknowledged that the rapid growth of AI and the need to build supporting infrastructure have complicated its ability to meet previous interim milestones and timelines.

item.title: Report: AI training data market is a fragmented cottage industry with brokers, resellers, and startups amid billion-dollar spending by frontier AI labs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The AI training data market consists of numerous small-scale operators including brokers, data sellers, and startups, supporting the development of AI through diverse and decentralized data sourcing. Despite hype on social media about easy profits, many participants are referral agents or resellers with limited proprietary technology, though the market still involves significant spending by leading AI labs. A notable example is Google's $10 million purchase of Spirit Airlines' internal business data for AI training after the airline's bankruptcy, highlighting the value of enterprise data that reflects real business operations. Companies like Mercor and Handshake AI have reached billion-dollar revenue levels by supplying expert-generated training data, and AI labs such as Anthropic report hundreds of millions in vendor costs for data quality and evaluation, underscoring the scale and complexity of this emerging market.

item.title: Researchers find attackers use inconspicuous inbox rules named "a", "cc", and " " to hide Microsoft 365 account takeovers
item.description: Attackers have been exploiting Microsoft 365 accounts by creating inbox rules with simple names like "a", "cc", and a single space character to conceal their takeover activities. These hidden rules allow unauthorized access and manipulation of email communications without immediate detection, enabling attackers to maintain control over compromised accounts.

item.title: Analysis finds only em dash usage clearly increased in Reddit posts from 2019-2022 to 2026, challenging common AI detection signs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing over five million Reddit text posts from 100 large subreddits between 2019-2022 and 2026 found that among 26 common indicators of AI-generated content, only the use of em dashes increased significantly. Other supposed AI telltale signs, such as specific words or phrases, did not show a clear rise beyond normal language drift, suggesting they are unreliable for identifying AI posts. The em dash appeared in 5.12% of posts in early 2026 compared to 0.69% in earlier years, about seven times more frequent, but this increase occurred gradually after ChatGPT's launch and cannot be directly linked to AI content. The research highlights the difficulty of distinguishing AI-generated Reddit posts based on linguistic cues alone, as language evolves and posting patterns shift over time.

item.title: Open-source Interviewer Assistant AI tool provides live coaching and answer scoring during video interviews via Microsoft Teams [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Interviewer Assistant is an open-source AI tool designed to support interviewers by joining video calls on Microsoft Teams, transcribing conversations live, and privately providing coaching through a web app. It scores candidate answers on correctness, depth, clarity, and relevance, suggests better responses, and proposes follow-up questions, all visible only to the interviewer. The tool integrates with Recall.ai for meeting access and transcription, and uses Anthropic Claude and Azure OpenAI models for analysis. It requires participant consent due to recording and transcription, is self-hosted, and the developer covers hosting costs while encouraging voluntary contributions. The project is available on GitHub with documentation and encourages community involvement for improvements and bug reports.

item.title: Author reflects on changing perspectives and implications of artificial intelligence before and after its integration [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article examines how thoughts and considerations about artificial intelligence have evolved from before its widespread adoption to after its integration into various fields. It discusses the shifting understanding of AI's impact and the broader implications across different contexts.

item.title: Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis meets with AI startup founders to discuss innovation and technology development [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis met with founders of artificial intelligence startups in Greece, emphasizing the country's commitment to advancing AI technology and supporting local innovation. The meeting highlights Greece's growing interest in fostering a vibrant AI ecosystem and encouraging the development of new technology ventures.

item.title: Nous Research launches Hermes Agent with Collective Wisdom feature for Microsoft Teams, enabling teams to share AI workflows securely [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Nous Research has introduced the open-source Hermes Agent, which companies can run directly inside Microsoft Teams to automate tasks like financial analysis and document drafting. The agent operates in isolated Azure Container Apps Sandboxes and allows employees to review AI-generated results within the chat interface. Hermes Agent's new Collective Wisdom feature automatically converts successful workflows into reusable skills that teams can share after review, keeping the knowledge within the company without contributing to external AI training data. The agent is widely used on OpenRouter, processing nearly two trillion tokens daily, and is part of Microsoft venture fund M12's portfolio, positioning itself as a key US open-source AI initiative.

item.title: AWS releases free local AWS Emulator built entirely by autonomous AI agents, covering over 200 services with published fidelity scores [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AWS has launched AWS Emulator, a free local implementation of more than 200 AWS services licensed under CC0, with all code generated and maintained by autonomous AI agents. The emulator runs as a single Rust binary and aims to support testing loops for coding agents by mimicking AWS APIs, though it does not evaluate IAM functionality. AWS publishes per-release fidelity scores comparing emulator behavior to real AWS, highlighting gaps and ongoing improvements. The project began with a simple prompt to an AI agent named Kiro, which iteratively built and tested service implementations against real AWS. Three agent teams now manage testing, issue detection, and fixes, with a gate process ensuring code quality and fidelity before merging. Early independent tests show varying fidelity across services, with DynamoDB, S3, and SQS passing 60-70% of tests, while others like CloudFormation score lower. Practitioners remain divided on trusting an emulator developed without human-written code review.

item.title: 16-year-old Henrijs Dandzbergs founds AI-guided missile startup Polemos Industries, joins Y Combinator to develop low-cost precision weapons for US and allies [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Henrijs Dandzbergs, a 16-year-old Latvian entrepreneur, founded Polemos Industries to create affordable, AI-guided missiles that can be launched from portable systems and resist jamming. He joined Y Combinator's fall 2026 cohort, becoming one of its youngest solo founders, aiming to reduce the "cost per kill" for military applications. Dandzbergs' interest in aerospace and defense was shaped by his education at an experimental school and the geopolitical tensions near his home country, especially the conflict in Ukraine. His startup focuses on optimizing targeted killing through advanced missile technology, reflecting his commitment to supporting US and allied military forces.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO signals AI industry growth potential and highlights market and regulatory challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

item.title: Anthropic faces strategic challenges after Claude Code-driven IPO as it plans next steps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

This transition period is critical as Anthropic seeks to capitalize on its IPO while navigating competitive pressures and evolving AI industry dynamics.

The timing of the statement coincides with Anthropic's IPO eve, drawing attention to debates within the AI community about the company's approach to safety and transparency. The signatories include prominent figures in AI and technology, underscoring the significance of the concerns raised.

item.title: SpaceX's AI unit denies liability for Grok-generated fake images of UK lawmaker, arguing such images cannot breach privacy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: SpaceX's AI division has denied liability for AI-generated images of a UK lawmaker created by its Grok model, asserting that obviously fake images do not constitute a privacy breach. The company argues that since the images are clearly fabricated, they should not be subject to privacy claims. This stance comes amid broader discussions about AI-generated content and privacy rights.

item.title: Apple is reportedly developing an AI agent to perform tasks on Macs, including app use, web browsing, and coding, with early-stage progress expected by late 2027 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Apple appears to be creating an AI agent capable of using a computer like a human, performing multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, and APIs. A recent job listing described the agent as able to browse the web, run commands, write and debug code, and choose appropriate tools while maintaining user privacy and Apple's quality standards. This development comes amid growing industry interest in AI agents from companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta. Bloomberg reports that Apple is also tightening controls on third-party AI agents by introducing warnings and requiring explicit user actions to grant full access to Macs in the upcoming macOS 27.3 update. While Apple has considered launching its own AI agent service by the end of 2027, the project remains in early stages and the company has not publicly commented on the initiative.

item.title: Anthropic's seven founders sold $1.95 billion in shares at $83 each during record $81.3 billion IPO [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic went public raising $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion from its seven founders who each sold about 3.4 million shares at $83 per share, netting roughly $280 million before fees and taxes. The company also raised nearly $105 billion through a combination of Class A common stock and $26 billion in special non-voting Class N stock purchased by major tech firms including Nvidia and Google. Amazon and Google now collectively own 28% of Anthropic following the IPO, with Google holding 13.4% and Amazon 14.6%. Despite the massive capital raise, Anthropic disclosed it faces over $1 trillion in infrastructure commitments through 2030, highlighting the high costs of operating its AI business.

item.title: Meta plans to price Muse Charm AI wearable at $300, spokesperson declines to confirm [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Meta is reportedly planning to sell its upcoming Muse Charm AI wearable device for $300, according to a report by The Information. The company has not denied the report but said it will share more details soon. Muse Charm is a physical AI companion that users can carry or wear, designed to interact through voice commands and questions. Meta has previously launched Muse, an AI assistant with customizable avatars, and is expanding into AI hardware with this device. The $300 price point is higher than some competitors but aligns with other AI wearables on the market.

item.title: Dario Amodei says Anthropic aims to cure all diseases and resist political pressure in record-breaking IPO [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated that the company plans to cure all diseases and maintain independence from political pressure as it prepares for a record-breaking initial public offering. The IPO marks a significant milestone for the AI startup, highlighting its ambitions in healthcare and technology sectors. Amodei emphasized the company's commitment to ethical AI development and its goal to leverage advanced AI models to address major health challenges. The IPO is expected to provide Anthropic with substantial capital to accelerate research and expand its influence in the AI industry.

item.title: Experts say recent US tech outages in airlines, banking, and productivity platforms reflect AI-driven legacy system vulnerabilities surfacing rapidly [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: In the past two weeks, major US businesses including Apple Pay, NASA, the FAA, and Microsoft experienced significant technical outages disrupting critical services. While officials and companies have ruled out cyberattacks or AI hacking as causes, cybersecurity experts suggest these incidents stem from AI exposing long-standing vulnerabilities in legacy systems during modernization efforts. Experts like Dave DeWalt and Anusha Iyer explain that AI tools are accelerating the discovery of security flaws, prompting rushed patches that temporarily disrupt services. The FAA outage, for example, may have resulted from attempts to upgrade telecommunications infrastructure that overwhelmed older hardware. These events highlight challenges in integrating modern AI-driven technologies with outdated systems without sufficient risk management. Senator Mark Warner and others view these disruptions as a warning about the rapid pace of AI adoption outstripping current security and operational controls. Industry leaders call for more cautious, phased AI integration with tighter segmentation and access controls to mitigate risks. Despite short-term disruptions, experts see opportunities for companies specializing in AI-driven vulnerability management and secure system modernization.

item.title: Google launches Gemini app feature to import chat history and preferences from other AI assistants via ZIP files and summaries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google's Gemini app now allows users to transfer their chat history, context, and preferences from other AI assistants. Users can export a ZIP file of their previous conversations and generate a summary of preferences to import into Gemini, enabling seamless continuation of past interactions without starting over.

item.description: Anthropic, an AI startup, has seen significant growth recently but faces potential financial challenges that could require it to seek new funding. Despite its current success, the company may need to secure additional capital to sustain its operations and development efforts. The situation reflects broader market pressures on AI startups balancing rapid expansion with financial sustainability.

item.title: WIRED discusses recent major outages affecting Microsoft, FAA, Chase, United, NSA, and Apple, officials deny cyberattacks amid public skepticism [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: WIRED's Uncanny Valley podcast examines a series of significant outages last week impacting major organizations including Microsoft, the FAA, Chase Bank, United Airlines, the NSA, and Apple. Officials have stated these disruptions were not caused by cyberattacks, though public suspicion remains high. The episode also covers Anthropic's record-setting IPO, Nvidia's first earnings report following Jensen Huang's resignation, and new U.S. regulations restricting Chinese companies from renting AI chips ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting. The discussion explores the causes behind the outages and why many initially blamed hackers or AI. It also analyzes the timing and implications of Anthropic's IPO amid recent political developments, Nvidia's leadership transition, and the U.S. administration's efforts to control AI technology access in the context of international relations with China.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid revelations of multiple affairs including one with alleged Chinese spy, raising U.S. national security concerns [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned following admissions of multiple extramarital affairs, one involving Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. officials of spying for China. This development comes amid heightened U.S.-China competition over AI infrastructure, where Nvidia plays a critical role as a leading AI chip supplier. Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company linked to the alleged spy, has been under investigation for potentially funneling Nvidia chips to China, with the U.S. Justice Department now involved. Despite the leadership turmoil, Nvidia reported strong quarterly earnings and announced it will cease selling its advanced H200 chips in China, signaling a tightening of compliance with U.S. export restrictions. Jensen Huang expressed willingness to return as CEO if the board deems it appropriate, supported by calls from industry figures, but Nvidia's interim leadership has ruled out reinstatement. The scandal underscores the intersection of personal misconduct and geopolitical risks in the tech sector's race for AI dominance.

item.title: Google Quantum AI demonstrates contextuality at scale on quantum processor, surpassing classical limits in coordination games and tasks up to 105 qubits
item.description: Google Quantum AI published research in Science showing that contextuality, a fundamental quantum property believed to power certain quantum algorithms, persists at scale on their quantum processor. Their qubits won a coordination game 98.3% of the time, exceeding the 88.9% classical limit, and outperformed classical strategies in tasks involving up to 105 qubits. This demonstration extends previous small-scale observations of contextuality to larger quantum systems and provides a sensitive method to detect subtle hardware errors. The findings support progress toward practical quantum computing applications in fields like chemistry and materials science.

item.title: Dario Amodei shifts from anti-war physicist to AI safety advocate, publicly promoting his approach to AI risk management [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
